4. The root cause can be one value or many values of that column. Include every value that materially drives the change, and nothing else.
5. Answer.

List every resource that is a root cause; include only root causes.

import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data.csv', parse_dates=['date'])
sub = df[df.account_id=='YxSxqn0'].copy()
anomaly = pd.Timestamp('2025-10-13')
base = sub[(sub.date >= '2025-10-06') & (sub.date < anomaly)]
anom = sub[sub.date == anomaly]

# residual check: exclude the two combos, what's left of the change?
m1 = (sub.cloud_service=='yNfDD')&(sub.application=='WIy')
m2 = (sub.cloud_service=='9Mj5O')&(sub.application=='gKM')
resid = sub[~(m1|m2)]
r_base = resid[(resid.date>='2025-10-06')&(resid.date<anomaly)]
r_anom = resid[resid.date==anomaly]
print("residual total change:", r_anom.unblended_cost.sum() - r_base.groupby('date')['unblended_cost'].sum().mean())

for col in ['csp','cloud_service','application','instance_family']:
    b = r_base.groupby(col)['unblended_cost'].sum()/7
    a = r_anom.groupby(col)['unblended_cost'].sum()
    chg = (a-b).dropna().abs().sort_values(ascending=False)
    print(col, "max residual |change|:", chg.head(3).round(1).to_dict())
